question: Since the A6000 is ~45x faster single-stream, does batching the phone [0,8) head raise its throughput?

measured.note: 13.4x single-stream; forward time only 204->285ms from B8->B32, still scaling

19.9x single-stream; +13% tput over B48 (diminishing, compute-bound); B64 is the binary's --driver-batch arg cap. b32 re-measured here at 112.5 tok/s == prior 112.2 -> prompt length does not affect decode throughput

extended_sweep.ceiling_reason: layersplit.cpp arg validator rejects --driver-batch > 64; also n_ubatch capped at min(n_batch,512) requires prompt_tokens*batch <= 512 (B64 needs a <=8-token prompt). B96/B128 need a host+phone rebuild.
extended_sweep.saturation: diminishing returns B32->B48->B64 (+32%, +13%); weight buffer fixed 3454 MiB, missing_buffer=0 at every batch; forward time grows ~linearly with batch in this region (compute-bound), throughput still rising but flattening

correctness_resolution.verdict: batched decode is CORRECT; the earlier token_match=False was a WRONG-REFERENCE artifact, not a bug
evidence: batch 1 (deterministic): phone [0,8)+[8,48) is BIT-EXACT vs mono (Stage B) -> the split is numerically correct

the A6000 FULL model ALONE gives batch-size-dependent greedy paths (b2 drops 1, b4 drops 2 tokens vs single-stream) -> float non-associativity in batched attention/GEMM is inherent, not phone-specific
phone route batch-2 stream0 == GPU full-model batch-2 stream0 EXACTLY -> the phone head matches the full model at the same batch

detokenised output is coherent text at every batch (single: '...utilization.

thought'; batch4: '...utilization.

<|channel>thought') -> valid completions, not corruption
correctness_resolution.why_no_reference_is_all_true: three distinct float-reduction orders (single-stream GPU, batched GPU, batched HTP) flip greedy argmax at near-ties; greedy BIT-matching is the wrong correctness test for batched inference. Certify via activation rel_L2 / coherence instead (batch-1 activation-exactness already does).
correctness_resolution.status: THROUGHPUT_AND_DECODE_CORRECTNESS_CERTIFIED (greedy bit-identity is not expected across batch/hardware)

findings.batched_multiseq_htp_decode_works: yes with FA on (the S1 hang was the GGML_DECODE_NO_FA path), coherent output at all batches
findings.kernel_regime: bandwidth-bound to ~B4 (forward flat), gently compute-bound B8-B32 (forward 204->285ms for 4x work -> still ~2.9x more throughput); ceiling not yet reached at B32

revised_overlap_math.note: b64 (167 tok/s, the binary cap) is certified; batching lifts one phone from 2.2% (single-stream) to 45% of the A6000, and the TWO phones on hand carry ~90% -> ~13.7% realised GPU-board decode saving, at/above the 13.3% mix ceiling (which is capped by [0,8) depth s(8)=15.1%). Two batched phones now essentially cover full decode-head offload against a saturated A6000; the ~40-phone single-stream fleet collapses to ~2-3.

caveats: OP15/HTP0 batched HEAD throughput ONLY. Phone energy UNKNOWN. Measured phone-only (host tail on GPU); Stage D showed the phone runs clean alongside a busy A6000, so the batched rate should hold under concurrency (unverified).
throughput = batch / forward_time; forward_time = stage_a_us_p50 / n_gen (includes a small prefill share, so a mild upper bound on per-decode forward).
B=2 is reproducibly token-incorrect; B4/B8 are token-correct vs mono. Fix the B=2 multi-seq alignment before trusting arbitrary batch sizes.
revised phone counts still say one phone is throughput-limited; batching cuts the fleet needed from ~40 to ~9, not to 1.
